# stock-clearance.ai

> stock-clearance.ai is a global B2B marketplace where international buyers source surplus, overstock, clearance, liquidation and stock-lot inventory directly from verified Chinese suppliers in the Yiwu Wuyuai market and major China industrial belts (Zhejiang, Guangdong, Jiangsu). Buyers browse live lots, request quotes, and trade wholesale with no middlemen.

## What it is
- A B2B clearinghouse for excess inventory, not a retail store.
- Suppliers post stock lots with photos, quantity, original and clearance price, and MOQ.
- Buyers inquire and negotiate directly with suppliers.
- Inventory spans apparel, electronics, home goods, pet supplies, toys, and shoes & socks.

## Market reports (B2B sourcing guides)
- [Market reports index](https://www.stock-clearance.ai/reports/index.html): all published buying guides and category reports, updated continuously.
- [Home storage & organization stock lots — the B2B buying guide](https://www.stock-clearance.ai/reports/home-storage-organization-stock-lot-guide.html): where storage-box and organizer surplus comes from (colour discontinuations, cancelled exports, chain overstocks, re-graded returns), indicative USD 0.3–1.2/pc plastic bins to USD 3–10/pc wooden storage furniture, A/B/mixed grading with fabric odour and moisture checks, the set-completeness trap on modular organizers, and a five-step pre-payment checklist.
- [Garden & outdoor products stock lots — the B2B seasonal buying guide](https://www.stock-clearance.ai/reports/garden-outdoor-products-stock-lot-guide.html): why garden surplus runs on the season clock (summer goods turn surplus September–November), counter-season vs in-season buying trade-offs, indicative USD 0.2–1.5/pc planters to USD 5–20/pc patio furniture, UV-aging/rust/fabric-degradation checks, solar and battery compliance lines, and a five-step pre-payment checklist.
- [Customs clearance for stock lots — the B2B import & logistics guide](https://www.stock-clearance.ai/reports/customs-clearance-stock-lot-import-guide.html): why clearance cargo gets extra customs scrutiny, per-line HS classification for mixed lots (several to a few dozen tariff lines per container), declaring the real transaction value instead of under-invoicing, the documentation pack (invoice, packing lists per supplier, origin certificates, product certificates), destination-market entry requirements (EU EORI, US ISF 10+2, UKCA, GCC conformity), duty and tax math, Incoterms for stock deals (FOB as the workhorse, DDP as the riskiest) and a five-step pre-shipment clearance checklist.
- [Reselling stock lots — the B2B channel & margin guide](https://www.stock-clearance.ai/reports/reselling-stock-lots-channel-guide.html): why the exit must be planned before the purchase, the six resale channels (discount retail, wholesale distribution, online marketplaces, B-stock platforms, cross-border re-trade, live commerce), illustrative landed-cost-to-sell-through margin math, channel-fit by category, the 90-day velocity rule with lot segmentation and residue bundling, branded-surplus compliance notes (trademark exhaustion, no re-labelling) and a five-step channel checklist.
- [Stock lot inspection & payment terms — the B2B risk control guide](https://www.stock-clearance.ai/reports/stock-lot-inspection-payment-terms-guide.html): typical T/T structures (deposit around 30% plus balance before shipment or against B/L copy), company-account and milestone-linking payment rules, the three proofs before any deposit (carton photos, live warehouse video with handwritten date card, date of manufacture), third-party inspection typically USD 100–200 per man-day, how AQL sampling adapts to mixed-grade stock lots, supplier red flags and a five-step pre-payment checklist.
- [Seasonal stock lots — the B2B peak-season buying calendar guide](https://www.stock-clearance.ai/reports/seasonal-stock-lot-buying-calendar-guide.html): the month-by-month surplus calendar (Christmas décor late December–February, back-to-school July–September, summer goods September–November), why counter-season buying typically secures the deepest discounts, a counter-season vs in-season trade-off table, aging and licensed-character checks for old seasonal lots, and a five-step buying checklist.
- [Mixed container stock lots — the B2B guide to consolidating clearance cargo](https://www.stock-clearance.ai/reports/mixed-container-stock-lot-loading-guide.html): when one mixed FCL beats several LCL parcels (crossover around 14–15 CBM; LCL typically USD 20–60/CBM on major lanes), indicative 20ft/40ft/40ft HC capacity figures, the heavy–medium–light loading order with the door rule, moisture protection (desiccants, dunnage, dry-goods checks), the one-master-B/L plus per-supplier packing-list document pattern, and a five-step pre-shipping checklist.
- [Shoes overstock & footwear stock lots — the B2B buying guide](https://www.stock-clearance.ai/reports/footwear-shoes-overstock-stock-lot-guide.html): surplus sources (size-run breaks, forecast overproduction, cancelled export orders, last-season styles), indicative USD 0.5–2/pair sandals, USD 1.5–4/pair canvas, USD 3–8/pair sneakers, USD 5–12/pair boots, USD 4–10/pair dress shoes, the size-run trap (mid-sizes sell first), sole and box grading, branded-goods IP notes and a five-step pre-payment checklist.
- [Tableware & kitchenware stock lots — the B2B pricing guide](https://www.stock-clearance.ai/reports/tableware-kitchenware-stock-lot-pricing-guide.html): why decorated tableware strands by pattern (discontinued decor, holiday leftovers, rebranding), indicative USD 0.15–0.6/pc mugs, USD 3–15/set dinner sets, USD 0.5–2.5/set cutlery, USD 2–8/pc cookware, food-contact compliance (EU 1935/2004, EU 84/500/EC, FDA, LFGB), packing and drop-test checks for ceramic breakage, and a five-step pre-payment checklist.

## Frequently asked questions
- **How do I buy overstock and clearance stock from China?** Browse live lots on stock-clearance.ai, open a lot, and send an inquiry with your target quantity. Suppliers reply with pricing and shipping. All trade is wholesale B2B; there is no retail checkout.
- **What is the minimum order (MOQ)?** It varies by lot and is shown on each listing. Many surplus lots are available in single-pallet or single-carton quantities because the goods are already produced.
- **Do you ship worldwide?** Suppliers ship to global destinations via sea and air freight; logistics are arranged between buyer and supplier.
- **Are suppliers verified?** Listings show supplier contact (WhatsApp) and verification status where available; buyers transact directly with suppliers.
- **Is stock-clearance.ai a retailer?** No. It is a marketplace that connects global buyers with Chinese surplus-stock suppliers; it does not hold inventory or process payments.
